svg.title: The M5 chatbot test set-up in QA terms
svg.text: How the M5 chatbot was tested, in QA terms
Two check layers on every turn; the judge itself was tested before it was trusted.
turn: tools to call or avoid,
Comparison on the same 28 conversations: our two layers against four general DeepEval metrics (same judge model)
our 12 rules from the spec, turn by turn
not our rules: helpfulness, completeness, memory
flagged 0 of 14 (expected: not told the rules)
* e.g. internal codes shown to the member, the member's own dates stated as fact, a mistyped ID looked up before confirming. The point: general
metrics alone would have passed this bot, and the 4 conversations they did fail were the bot doing the right thing (required refusals).
Unit tests of the code and tooling: pytest, 104 tests, free
access check, chunking, prompt experiments, checks, judge plumbing, labels, compare.
They test our code, not the bot's replies; the replies are tested by the two layers above.
